reviews.comment: Dr. Bergbreiter is the best professor I have had at TAMU. He is incredibly knowledgeable and always available to help you learn. Tests are difficult but focus on really understanding the problem sets, and I would encourage people to read the textbook. He is an amazing resource though for academic and life advice!

As long as you read the textbooks, do the HW, and master the practice exams, you shouldn't get anything but an A. No need for any outside studying, lectures are not required, and he curves everyone to an A.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Hilarious--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bergbreiter teaches his course in a way that makes you as a student take real responsibility for your grade. The course is tough, but he will be on campus pretty much all the time available to help with any questions. You will regret not taking this course.

As an honors class, it's hard. The material covered will be more in depth and "concept based" than the other sections. This does not mean it's impossible though, it just takes lots of work to actually do well on exams. If you are passionate about the workings of ochem then take berg but for everyone else who struggles just take a regular section.

Bergbreiter is the best professor I've had. He's very understanding and REALLY wants you to succeed. Don't be afraid to ask for help or talk to him, he will work hard to help you! Exams are at night and he grades them in front of you, so that's scary. But he's so accessible I'm taking him for Ochem 2. Big curve and extra credit. READ THE TEXTBOOK

Dr. Bergbreiter is an awesome prof. His class is hard and took a lot of dedicated time, but if you put in the work, you'll get the grade. He wants you to succeed so bad, so if you are struggling or don't know what's going on, just go talk to him. He might be a little intimidating at first but don't let that stop you from asking questions. Take him.
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--EXTRA CREDIT--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: David E. Bergbreiter is the GOAT

not a good lecturer, very disorganized and bad at explaining things. his exams were so unnecessarily hard and confusing, i struggled so much in his class for ochem1 but then i took a different prof for ochem 2 and got a solid A. L prof

Professor Bergbreiter is the BEST professor I have ever had in my entire college experience. He is super helpful and inspiring. I am now a Psychology and Chemistry major because I realized that I truly love the chemistry subject. Yes the class is hard, but it is completely fair and you truly learn.

tough prof but prepares you for bich better than no other. problem sets are HARD & you will fail if you dont go to class and take quick notes off his chalkboard. I had to do a lot of self-teaching on my own to supplement lectures. 84% for A, drops lowest exam, and super available to help in office hrs. if you didnt take his 227, it's gonna be tough

He was a very hard grader, and you have to really understand, not just memorize to do well. If you didnt take him for ochem 1, dont take him for ochem 2 you will struggle. He writes everything on a chalkboard and is hard to follow. I had to go in for office hours and go to tutoring to be able to pass this class. He will prepare you well for biochem

Do NOT take him. Writes on the chalkboard during his lectures and I didn't learn a thing. The textbook provided is not very helpful and you'll be tested over additional material he only briefly covers. Also made derogatory comments towards me and made fun of me the entire semester when I would ask for help. Worst professor I've taken.

Berg is one of the smartest and most well-respected chemistry professors at TAMU. He is extremely knowledgeable, but that may be his biggest downfall. During lectures he gets off topic and rambles about chemistry way above our knowledge level. There are weekly problem sets and AKTIV. Tests are extremely fair. You have to put in the work.

Problem weekly, harder than need to be. Has help sessions before problem set 8pm. AKTIV. Tests are graded hard. First exam got 52, I thought I got A since I studied hard.He takes off lot of partial credit on mechanisms. Know mechanisms! OCHEM 2 has spectrums which are fun. The mechanisms are not fun. Allows index card cheat sheet. Office hours too.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Get ready to read--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Berg is probably the only professor I've had that can lecture off an example from his head. Extremely knowledgeable in the field of chemistry and available on most days. Hard psets but he'll help you with them and make sure you understand it.Your best resource for bergs class is berg himself. Very spontaneous humor and a little too blunt for a prof

Out of all of the professors I've had, he is by far the most accessible. He typically hosts his own review session once a week at night, where he gives homework help for >3 hours. Additionally, he can be found in his office almost 24/7. One thing to note is he is a chalkboard lecturer, but that has not been a big deal imo.

In class, Bergbreiter is very funny but his lectures tend to be difficult to follow. Reading chapters beforehand is a smart idea. Overall, you will probably learn more outside of class, but Bergbreiter is available almost 24/7 outside of class (even weekends). 3 Exams, 1 Final, 10pg paper, weekly problem sets & Aktiv hw. Very forgiving grade system

He does not give notes or provides powerpoint. He scribbles on a chalkboard and goes so fast. Doesnt elaborate and expects you to remember everything from gen chem. He's a nice man though and he lives in his office, but dont expect to keep up in lecture.

I took Bergbreiter for his Organic 1 and his Majors Organic 2, but honestly, with the rigor that he teaches, his sections might as well be the major's sections. Extremely talented, educated, and respected in his field. Phenomenal Lecturer, an understanding person, available any time, and a forgiving grading system. He inspired me to learn Organic
Dont do it.

If you do not learn well from drawing on a literal chalkboard without any form of structured notes, this is not the prof for you. Lectures were hard to follow and writing on board tended to be messy. But he made it up with many review sessions and opportunities for extra help. Tests were difficult but always had opportunities for extra credit.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: Dr. Bergbreiter is a very good and humorous organic chemistry professor. He has a forgiving grading system, and always makes the effort to remain accessible outside of class. This makes it quite possible do do well in his class. However, his lectures can be confusing at times, but his homework assignments and exam reviews align with his exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: By far the most accessible professor outside of class. His grading is very forgiving, there's lots of extra credit, and there's a term paper that essentially replaces an exam grade. The problem sets are difficult but prepare you well for the exams. My only complaint is that it's hard to read his handwriting sometimes on the board.
reviews.ratingTags: EXTRA CREDIT--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: I had Dr. Bergbreiter as a replacement professor for CHEM 227 when Dr. Waas had to step down for the semester. Dr. Bergbreiter will challenge you in ways you haven't imagined. However, he is VERY accessible outside of class and will offer so much help! He is a little mean so you'll need some thicker skin.

By far the most accessible prof at A&M, he provides so much resources for you to do well. Exams are challenging because they require you know the material, but they are not tricky, in fact they are very straightforward. Lectures are interesting even with how complicated they are. Grading scale for the class is very forgiving.
Great man. Truly cares about the well being of his students and constantly gives great personalized feedback so you know where you stand.

I love Bergbreiter; a great lecturer and a bit funny. He's very caring towards students and then succeeding, providing difficult problem sets similar to exams (exams are easier), extra credit opportunities, and to top it off he's available at almost anytime during the day plus his night help and review sessions. He's not a turd just very blunt

Reminded me a lot of Walter White for some reason. I loved him though. He gave LOTS of extra credit which absolutely saved my grade. I didn't learn much in his lectures, but he made ochem a little fun. He was hilarious and made the early class enjoyable. And the final was multiple choice.

Dr. Bergbreiter is one of my favorite prof at a&m. He makes the material fun to learn, and he is accessible basically on any given time of the day. His problem sets are difficult, but it prepares you well for the exams. He has lot of grading events to ensure you are doing well in the class. Exams are not easy but it is very straight forward.
reviews.ratingTags: Tough grader--Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He's a great person, cares about his students and grades. He will tell you exactly what you need to do to do well in his class, and is probably the most accessible prof at tamu. Attend his help sessions, I swear you will learn more there. His test are probably the hardest ochem test but the practice exams and problem set are similar.

It's organic chemistry, it's a difficult class. But the requirement for an A is very doable. If you want to do well in the class, you need to go to his office. He comes off as not willing to help, but he is very much willing to help on his problem sets and his exams, which are difficult. You have to be committed to ochem for his class

He scribbles on the chalkboard and by the time he's finished, he moves on to the next problem. I'm sure he knows what he is doing, but he is not very good at explaining things. He is bad at explaining and his exams are similar to practice exams but you have to know what you're doing. Even watching other professors videos was not enough.

He is very old school so basically scribbles on a chalkboard. He is knowledgeable just doesn't do a very good job explaining what he teaches. No PowerPoint or notes are provided. He does have a term paper that can be used to replace 1 exam. He lives in his office so he can always help if you have questions. Practice exams and PS similar to exams.
Don't do it.

The best prof I've ever had. His exams and problem sets are rough and he knows that. There are four midterm exams and one final taking up 500 points and your other 300 points are from homework assignments and a term paper. He drops the lowest grade set (more than likely a test grade). He is the most accessible prof if you ever need help. TAKE HIM!

if you put in the effort, youll be just fine! it may seem hard but thats because youre learning the material rather than memorizing- and thatll make it so much easier later on!! also hes super accessible outside of class so go talk to him whenever you can- its super helpful!!!

Dr. Bergbreiter is one of the best professors I have had here at A&M. His class isn't the easiest, but he does want everyone to succeed. There are plenty of resources outside of class and you just have to use them! There are a ton of help sessions and office hours to get help. Also, he drops an exam grade!

If I had to retake this class I'd definitely sign up for Berg again. Although his tests were rough (mostly application qs) it's clear that Berg isn't out to get you. He wants his students to succeed, but you really have to put a lot of work into this class. He drops your lowest test grade! (OWL/Attendance/Assignments together counted as a test)
reviews.ratingTags: Respected--Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Berg's class is pretty tough and he makes you work for your grade, but I feel like I got a lot out of it. Doesn't rely on memorization and drops a few grades (problem sets, owl). Gives an optional essay that can replace an exam. Exams are HARD but manageable if you put in the work the week before. Very accessible and helpful during help sessions!

I had to teach myself completely from the textbook and used his lectures mainly as a review before exams. The one thing I really like about his class is the grading. He drops a few grades so if you do bad on one exam or forget to do a hw assignment, it'll be ok, and major grades include hw and a term paper. His lecture style doesn't work for me tho
reviews.ratingTags: Get ready to read--Clear grading criteria

reviews.comment: Dr. Bergbreiter is AMAZING! He was always around to help, and will spend hours with you to make sure you understand the material. His lectures are really interesting and he often applies the material that we are learning to applications in the real world and even brought up current scientific breakthroughs. I highly recommend Dr. Bergbreiter.

I was nervous to take Organic Chemistry but Professor Bergbreiter's course made this subject one of my favorites. He uses humor and random, crazy examples for the important parts of lecture so that they are engrained in your memory. This class is definitely tough, but it was more about understanding the material rather than complete memorization.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Skip class? You won't pass.--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Bergbreiter seems intimidating at first, but once you get to know him, especially during office hours, he's not that bad of a person. He practically lives in his office, so office hours are flexible. Makes lectures really interesting and understandable. HW is super hard, but help from PLTL is available and definitely prepares us for exams.
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Amazing lectures

reviews.comment: Hes clearly a smart guy but as a student I found his class hard. The content covered in his section is much more than other sections since its for chem majors. As a person who switched majors and took chem 228 with a different prof I can confirm that his section is much harder.

Possibly the worst professor I've ever had in my college career. Students praise him which I really don't understand why. He's also really rude and arrogant, and honestly only cares about his research. Super inconsistent with grading especially on exams. I would not consider taking this prof unless you have to cause you're a "major." Avoid.

Prof. Bergbreiter is the perfect representation of a dedicated/inspirational professor is. I enjoyed his course (OChem) more than I thought. He is always clear and present to give feedback to each student in his class, and explains concepts clearly. He comes into the PLTL sessions regularly (even at 11pm!) and helps students solve the homework.

227 is hard, but you won't have to memorize anything with Berg. You will have to deeply understand the material, but PLTL and office hours will help greatly with that. He makes the homework hard so that you go get help and learn it. Tests are like the homework. VERY interesting lectures which feature real world applicable chemistry. Learned a lot
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Lots of homework--Accessible outside class

reviews.comment: He gives very entertaining lectures, however, they can be over your head at most times. I felt that his office hours were extremely beneficial! He is usually available, even on the weekends. His exams are difficult, but the problem sets do prepare you well as long as you understand them. PLTL is also very helpful. Just talk to him!
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: The best chemistry prof at tamu. Always in his office and will explain things for hours if you need it. No excuse not to do well when you can get plenty of help on any and all assignments. exams are challenging but contain nothing that has not been presented in class before
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--Accessible outside class--Skip class? You won't pass.

reviews.comment: Make sure you can fully explain every answer to the problem sets and the exams will be fine. The tests are hard because the questions are interesting and require both common sense and true understanding of the material. Do every single problem set. Hes almost ALWAYS available and will answer all questions thoroughly. Best prof, awesome guy
reviews.ratingTags: Gives good feedback--LOTS OF HOMEWORK--ACCESSIBLE OUTSIDE CLASS

reviews.comment: Bergbreiter is the king of analogies and the best organic professor at A&M. He makes class entertaining and is by far the most accessible professor I've ever had. Take advantage of his office hours, you can pretty much stop by any time. He makes you work hard but it's worth it. Reading the textbook before class helped me follow along in class.

Bergbreiter is a very excellent teacher. He knows how to keep students interested in what hes teaching and is consistently available outside of class. He cares if the students learn, is funny, and in my opinion is the best O Chem professor at A&M. The class is definitely hard but you will feel like you earned the grade you made in his class.

Dr. Bergbreiter is the best professor I have taken at Texas A&M. He is absolutely brilliant, and a fantastic teacher. He really cares about whether his students pass or fail, and puts a lot of time outside of class into helping his students learn. It is by no means easy, but he is the best Ochem prof out there.

He is best prof I have had, but if you are just looking for an A in organic go elsewhere. I probably could've had an easy A taking another class, but I worked hard for my B in the class and I don't regret it because I learned so much. He is so incredibly helpful and he devotes so much time to be around to answer homework questions late at night.

Very difficult course, but worth the hard work because you actually learn the material.  He is always willing to go above and beyond, and will give you as much help as you ask for.  I took him for both semesters of organic chemistry, even though I knew I could probably make a better grade with an easier professor.

Very nice to undergrads, very mean to grad students.  Looks like a cross between mortician and homeless person.  Very, very, intellegent.  Breadth and scope of his chemical knowledge and intuition is truely astonishing.  Not very creative as far as research direction, also stifles creativity of graduate students working for him.  If you wourk for him you WILL be his ****, this is both bad (obviously) and good.  He is feared/reveared not only by students but also by most faculty and is very protective.

I had him for Organic I and II and Polymer Chemistry.  Pros:  He's a great lecturer, he really knows his stuff, and he's pretty funny.   He forces you to actually understand the material, rather than just memorize it and then regurgitate in on the exam.  Cons:  He can be rude, pompous, and has personal hygene issues.
